note: Advisory only. Hand-curated statements about providers' publicly documented data practices (training on customer API data, retention windows, subprocessor lists, enterprise-tier deltas) as of each fact's retrieval date. Never legal advice; never auto-filled from upstream feeds; never influences verdicts. Each entry carries its own 'reviewed' date; undocumented facts are recorded as null (explicitly unknown), never guessed.

entry.training_default: yes | no | opt-out | null (whether the provider trains on customer API data by default)
entry.retention: free-text retention window for API inputs/outputs, or null when not publicly documented
entry.subprocessors: {url, locator, retrieved} link to the subprocessor list, or null when none found
entry.enterprise_tier: free-text note on whether an enterprise/commercial tier changes the answers, or null
entry.reviewed: ISO-8601 date this entry was last human-reviewed
entry.citations: per-fact {url, locator, retrieved}; every non-null fact MUST carry one

openai.retention: Abuse-monitoring logs retained up to 30 days by default; application state varies by endpoint (Responses API stores 30 days when store=true; some endpoints until deleted). Zero Data Retention or Modified Abuse Monitoring excludes customer content from abuse logs for approved customers.

subprocessors.locator: Linked from the data controls guide ('OpenAI uses sub-processors to provide its services')

openai.enterprise_tier: Zero Data Retention and Modified Abuse Monitoring are subject to prior approval by OpenAI and acceptance of additional requirements (contact sales); Enterprise Key Management (BYOK) is available for application state.

training_default.locator: 'As of March 1, 2023, data sent to the OpenAI API is not used to train or improve OpenAI models (unless you explicitly opt in)'; per-endpoint table shows 'Data used for training: No'

retention.locator: 'Abuse monitoring logs ... retained for up to 30 days' and per-endpoint 'Storage requirements and retention controls' table

enterprise_tier.locator: 'Currently, these controls are subject to prior approval by OpenAI and acceptance of additional requirements'; Enterprise Key Management (EKM) section

subprocessors.locator: Commercial Terms of Service section C routes data processing through the DPA (which governs subprocessors); no standalone public subprocessor page was reachable at review time

training_default.locator: Section B (Customer Content): 'Anthropic may not train models on Customer Content from Services.'

google_gemini.retention: Paid Services: prompts and responses logged for a limited period solely for detecting/preventing Prohibited Use Policy violations; Grounding with Google Search/Maps stores prompts and outputs for 30 days. Unpaid Services: content may be used to improve Google products (do not submit confidential data).

subprocessors.locator: Google Cloud Platform Subprocessors page (last modified August 19, 2026 at review time)

google_gemini.enterprise_tier: The paid/unpaid split is the effective tier boundary: unpaid Gemini API quota and free-tier AI Studio use submissions to improve Google products; EEA/Switzerland/UK users get the paid (no-training) rules even on unpaid Services.

training_default.locator: Paid Services - How Google Uses Your Data: 'Google doesn't use your prompts ... or responses to improve our products' (Unpaid Services section states the opposite for free usage)

retention.locator: Paid Services: 'Google logs prompts and responses for a limited period of time, solely for detecting and preventing violations of the Prohibited Use Policy'; Grounding sections: 'store prompts ... for thirty (30) days'

enterprise_tier.locator: Unpaid Services - How Google Uses Your Data; 'If you're in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, or the United Kingdom, the terms under Paid Services apply to all Services'

azure_openai.retention: Models are stateless: no prompts or completions are stored in the model. Stateful features (Responses API, Assistants Threads, Stored completions, Files/vector stores) persist data in the resource's Azure geography until deleted. Abuse monitoring stores prompt/completion samples only when flagged, in logically separated per-resource stores; modified abuse monitoring turns this off for approved customers.

subprocessors.locator: Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum, linked from the data-privacy article intro

azure_openai.enterprise_tier: Modified abuse monitoring requires application and approval; customers can verify logging is off via the ContentLogging=false capability attribute in the Azure portal/CLI.

training_default.locator: 'prompts and completions are NOT used to train any generative AI foundation models without your permission or instruction'; 'The models are stateless: no prompts or completions are stored in the model'

retention.locator: Sections 'Generating completions...' (stateless models), 'Data storage for Models sold by Azure features', and 'Preventing abuse' (flagged-sample storage, logical separation, modified abuse monitoring)

enterprise_tier.locator: 'How can a customer verify if data storage for abuse monitoring is off?' (ContentLogging=false); 'managed customers may apply to modify abuse monitoring'

azure_foundry.retention: Models are stateless: no prompts or completions are stored in the model. Stateful features (Responses API, Assistants Threads, Stored completions, Files/vector stores) persist data in the resource's Azure geography until deleted; Global and DataZone deployment types may process prompts/responses across regions within their scope. Abuse monitoring stores prompt/completion samples only when flagged, in logically separated per-resource stores; modified abuse monitoring turns this off for approved customers.

subprocessors.locator: Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum, which governs data processing by Models sold by Azure (linked from the data-privacy article intro)

azure_foundry.enterprise_tier: Modified abuse monitoring requires application and approval; customers can verify logging is off via the ContentLogging=false capability attribute in the Azure portal/CLI. Catalog scope caveat: Foundry also serves partner/community model catalogs whose own terms may differ — verify per deployed model.

training_default.locator: 'Your prompts (inputs) and completions (outputs), your embeddings, and your training data ... are NOT used to train any generative AI foundation models without your permission or instruction'; 'The models are stateless: no prompts or completions are stored in the model'

retention.locator: Sections 'Generating completions...' (stateless models, geography processing incl. Global/DataZone), 'Data storage for Models sold by Azure features', and 'Preventing abuse' (flagged-sample storage, logical separation, modified abuse monitoring)

subprocessors.locator: Article intro: 'Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum (https://aka.ms/DPA), which governs data processing by Models sold by Azure'

enterprise_tier.locator: 'How can a customer verify if data storage for abuse monitoring is off?' (ContentLogging=false); 'managed customers may apply to modify abuse monitoring'

aws_bedrock.retention: Zero data retention by default (zero operator access + ZDR security model): Bedrock does not store model inputs or outputs. Exceptions retain inputs/outputs up to 30 days for automated abuse detection (e.g. classifier-flagged traffic of certain hosted OpenAI GPT-5.x models; Claude Fable 5 retains up to 30 days). Setting data_retention_mode to 'none' enforces zero retention account/project-wide.
aws_bedrock.enterprise_tier: Some models (Claude Mythos 5, Claude Fable 5) require opting into provider_data_share, which retains and shares inference data with Anthropic for up to 30 days; full ZDR access for models requiring retention is evaluated per-account/per-model via the AWS account team.

retention.locator: Data retention modes table ('none': 'No request or response data is written to durable storage'); 'What data is retained and for how long' (30-day abuse-detection retention)

enterprise_tier.locator: 'For Anthropic Claude Fable 5, inputs and outputs will be retained for up to 30 days ... you must opt in to sharing retained traffic with Anthropic'; ZDR access section of the data-retention page

deepseek.retention: Personal data is collected, processed and stored in the People's Republic of China (controller: Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd.). No fixed retention window is published: data is retained 'for as long as necessary to provide our Services and for the other purposes set out in this Privacy Policy', then destroyed, deleted or anonymised when no longer required. No zero-data-retention tier or enterprise no-train arrangement is documented.
deepseek.enterprise_tier: No self-serve API opt-out mechanism or enterprise training carve-out is documented; the privacy policy describes a right to opt out of model-training use of your personal data at policy level. The Open Platform Terms of Service defer personal-data handling back to the privacy policy rather than exempting paid API traffic.

training_default.locator: Privacy Policy (updated 2026-02-10), purposes section: personal data processed 'to improve and develop the Services and to train and improve our technology, such as our machine learning models and algorithms', with a described right to opt out of such use; no API-specific carve-out

retention.locator: 'To provide you with our services, we directly collect, process and store your Personal Data in People's Republic of China'; retention 'for as long as necessary to provide our Services', destroyed/deleted/anonymised when no longer required

enterprise_tier.locator: Open Platform Terms of Service (effective 2026-04-29): personal-data handling defers to the Privacy Policy; no separate exemption for developer API inputs

moonshot.retention: Input/output content is retained while your account is active (privacy policy: 'account, input, and payment information are retained while your account is active'); violation-related information until resolved. Servers located in Singapore; cross-border transfers use appropriate safeguards.
moonshot.enterprise_tier: Restrictions on training use of Customer Content are available via enterprise arrangements or separate written agreements with Moonshot AI (ToS section 4); without such an agreement, Customer Content may be used to provide, maintain, develop, support, and improve the Services.

training_default.locator: Terms of Service section 4 (Content): 'We may use Content to provide, maintain, develop, support, and improve the Services ... Customer who requires restrictions on the use of Customer Content for training or improving Moonshot AI models may contact Moonshot AI to discuss available enterprise arrangements'

retention.locator: Privacy Policy section 6 (Retention): 'account, input, and payment information are retained while your account is active'; section 10: 'We store the information we collect in secure servers located in Singapore'

enterprise_tier.locator: Terms of Service section 4: enterprise arrangements or separate written agreements restrict training use of Customer Content

alibaba_dashscope.retention: Member Content (inputs and outputs) is processed on the customer's behalf; Alibaba Cloud deletes data per customer instructions on deletion/termination, subject to backup/disaster-recovery retention windows and legal-hold requirements (Product Terms 4.48.1(g)(iv)). Processing/storage location follows where Alibaba Cloud maintains Model Studio facilities and may differ from the customer's location.
alibaba_dashscope.enterprise_tier: Training-use restrictions are the default posture: Alibaba Cloud will not use Member Content to develop or improve Model Studio models unless the customer separately provides consent. Third-party models listed in Model Studio carry their own third-party terms that the customer must review separately.

training_default.locator: Section 4.48.1(e) (Model Studio): 'Alibaba Cloud will not use your Member Content to develop or improve the models on Model Studio, unless you separately provide your consent.'

retention.locator: Section 4.48.1(g)(iv) (deletion on instruction subject to backup/legal retention) and 4.48.1(g)(viii) (processing location where facilities are maintained)

enterprise_tier.locator: Section 4.48.1(e) (no model development/improvement on Member Content without separate consent) and 4.48.2 (third-party model services under separate third-party terms)

tencent_hunyuan.retention: TokenHub Privacy Policy Module: Configuration Data and Diagnostic and Usage Data (explicitly including 'output information') are 'generally retain[ed] ... for up to 30 days after your task request' for feature provision and troubleshooting, and may be retained longer (for example as long as you use the Features) for billing. Whether raw input prompts fall inside this scope is not explicit in the document.
tencent_hunyuan.note: Scope caveat: the cited retention window governs Tencent-as-controller configuration/diagnostic data; no explicit statement about training on customer inference inputs was found in the TokenHub Privacy Policy Module or Terms of Service at review time.

retention.locator: PRIVACY POLICY MODULE section 6 (DATA RETENTION), last updated 2026-08-13: 'we generally retain information for up to 30 days after your task request ... but may process or retain such data for a longer period (for example as long as you use the Features) for billing purposes'; section 3 includes 'output information' in Diagnostic and Usage Data

zhipu.retention: Personal information is stored within China only ('目前我们不会跨境传输或存储您的个人信息' — no cross-border transfer or storage at present), retained for the minimum period necessary for the stated purposes. On deletion, service expiry or termination a buffer period applies (per product docs), after which all data including cached and backup copies is deleted; deletion is irreversible.

subprocessors.locator: Section 三(一) shared third-party SDK/API table: Alipay face-verification and web payment APIs, WeChat Native Pay (Tenpay), Sensors Analytics (behaviour analytics), NetEase Qiyu (customer support), Aliyun SMS/mail push, Baidu Cloud SMS — each with the personal-info fields collected and purpose; covers the platform's account/payment/analytics surface

training_default.locator: User Agreement (effective 2025-05-20) section 三.9(1): uploaded data belongs to the user and '除执行您的服务要求外，不会进行任何未获授权的使用及披露' (no unauthorised use or disclosure beyond executing your service requests). Carve-out disclosed: Privacy Policy sections 二.7(4)/四.10 reserve anonymised derivatives for '机器学习或模型算法训练' (machine learning / model algorithm training) without further consent — identifiable content is not used; anonymised data may be.

retention.locator: Section 五(一) storage location (China only, no cross-border transfer at present); section 五(二) retention for the minimum necessary period; User Agreement section 三.9(3): buffer-period storage after deletion/expiry, then all copies including caches and backups deleted

github_copilot.retention: Varies by Copilot product/feature: the editor experience transmits prompts only to generate suggestions in real time and deletes them once suggestions are generated (not stored at rest without permission); retention exceptions include CLI/tool prompts, customised private language models, and alternative data-handling configurations. Per-product documentation governs each feature's exact window.
github_copilot.enterprise_tier: Tier/terms split: volume-licensing customers are governed by the GitHub Generative AI Services Terms (section 3: 'GitHub will not use Inputs or Outputs to train generative AI models, unless you have given us documented instructions to do so'); Copilot Business/Enterprise purchased directly from GitHub prior to 2026-03-05 remain under the deprecated Product-Specific Terms; individual users fall under the GitHub Terms of Service AI-features section.

training_default.locator: GitHub Generative AI Services Terms (Version March 2026) section 3 (Use of Data for Model Training): 'GitHub will not use Inputs or Outputs to train generative AI models, unless you have given us documented instructions to do so'

retention.locator: Deprecated Copilot Product Specific Terms section 6.A ('Prompts are transmitted only to generate Suggestions in real-time, are deleted once Suggestions are generated, and are not used for any other purpose') and 6.B (retention exceptions); superseded terms retained as the clearest per-feature retention statement — current governing document is the Generative AI Services Terms, whose section 6 defers retention details to product documentation

enterprise_tier.locator: Section 1 applicability (volume licensing vs personal customers vs Microsoft purchases); deprecation note on the Product-Specific Terms effective 5 March 2026

meta_llama.retention: Content and Usage Data retained as needed to provide the Services, for legal compliance, in connection with Meta's rights under the terms, when systems flag data for a potential policy violation, and for security/safety/abuse/policy review. No fixed retention window is published.

subprocessors.locator: Meta's published subprocessor list, referenced from Model API Terms of Service section 5.1 (Standard Services processor terms); may be updated by Meta from time to time

meta_llama.enterprise_tier: Tier split: Standard Services — 'Meta will not use Content from Standard Services to train Meta Models' (section 5.1). Discounted Services (discounted model tier) — content MAY be used to train, develop and improve Meta AI models by default, disassociated from your account/key before training use (section 6.1); traffic requiring no-training must use Standard Services.

training_default.locator: Model API Terms of Service section 5.1: 'Meta will not use Content from Standard Services to train Meta Models' (updated 2026-08-21)

retention.locator: Section 4.4 (Retention): five enumerated retention bases; no fixed window published

enterprise_tier.locator: Section 6.1 (Discounted Services): 'You agree that Meta may use your Content to train, develop, evaluate, and improve Meta's artificial intelligence models, products, and services', disassociation steps before training use; section 6.2 directs confidential traffic to Standard Services

nvidia_nim.retention: NVIDIA's general privacy policy: customer and enterprise personal data erased after more than five years without engagement; transfers to the US under Standard Contractual Clauses with EU-U.S./Swiss-U.S./UK Data Privacy Framework certification. NIM-API-specific inference-data terms were not retrievable at review time.

retention.locator: Data Retention section: 'We erase customer and enterprise personal data if there has been no engagement with you for more than five years'; Cross-Border Data Transfer section (SCCs, Data Privacy Framework)

xiaomi_mimo.retention: Personal information retained only as long as necessary for the stated purposes or as required by law; deleted or anonymised once the purpose is fulfilled, on erasure request, or on service termination (subject to legal-hold isolation).
xiaomi_mimo.enterprise_tier: Token Plan subscribers use a dedicated CN base URL (token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com) with tp- keys instead of the pay-as-you-go global endpoint; data-storage region selection is available on request, subject to compliance review and additional fees (service agreement 1.1).

training_default.locator: Section 3.1 (Collection of personal information from you): 'Xiaomi will not use the content you provide for model training or any other purposes.'

retention.locator: Section 6 (How long will your personal information be stored?): retained for the purposes described, deleted or anonymised after fulfilment/erasure/termination except where law requires isolation

enterprise_tier.locator: Section 1.1 (data storage regions selectable on request, subject to compliance and additional fees) and section 4.4 (services outside the Chinese Mainland store data on servers in Europe and Singapore); Token Plan host per the First API Call quickstart

vertex_ai.retention: Per-feature retention conditions on the generative-AI platform: prompt logging for abuse monitoring applies unless an exemption is requested; Grounding with Search keeps derived queries up to 3 days and Grounding with Maps stores prompts/outputs 30 days (neither can be disabled); request-response logging and Live-API session resumption are opt-in (24h TTL); published Gemini models cache customer data in-memory for 24 hours, project-isolated, not at rest. Zero data retention is achievable by configuration.

training_default.locator: Service Specific Terms 'Training Restriction': 'Google won't use your data to train or fine-tune any AI/ML models without your prior permission or instruction' — applies to all managed models on the generative-AI platform, GA and pre-GA

retention.locator: Zero-data-retention page (last updated 2026-08-21): abuse-monitoring prompt logging with exception path; Grounding with Search (3-day derived queries) and Maps (30-day prompts/outputs) storage cannot be disabled; opt-in request-response logging and Live-API session resumption (24h); in-memory caching of inputs/outputs/derived data, project-level isolation, 24h TTL, 'does not violate zero data retention', disableable at project level

fireworks_ai.retention: Zero data retention by default for inference on open models: prompt and generation data exist only in volatile memory for the duration of the request, absent explicit opt-in (e.g. FireOptimizer logging). Exception: the Response API with store=True (its default) retains stored conversation data for 30 days, then auto-deletes; store=False or the DELETE endpoint is immediate. Non-content metadata (token counts) is logged.

subprocessors.locator: Named in the Fireworks DPA §6.2 as the canonical list of Authorised Sub-processors, with 30 days' change notice via Trust Center subscription (www.fireworks.ai/dpa)

fireworks_ai.enterprise_tier: Enterprise admins can enforce the zero-retention policy org-wide (rejecting requests that would persist or log content); the standard DPA (with SCCs/UK/Swiss addenda) is incorporated into the Terms for all customers (ToS §2.4), not enterprise-only.

training_default.locator: Terms of Service (last updated 2026-07-01) §3.6 'Zero Data Retention': 'We will not use your Content to train our own models or to improve the Service'

retention.locator: 'Zero data retention': prompt/generation data 'exist only in volatile memory for the duration of the request' without opt-in; 'Response API data retention': with store=True 'all stored conversation data is automatically deleted after 30 days'

enterprise_tier.locator: 'Enterprise account admins can additionally turn on the Zero Data Retention policy to reject requests and jobs that would persist or log customer content'

together_ai.retention: Stored by default with no fixed window: prompts and responses persist in user history until the user deletes them ('By default, Together stores the prompts you send and the responses models return, and may use them for product improvements'). Self-serve Zero Data Retention in Privacy & Security settings disables storage of prompts/responses ('not persisted to non-volatile storage'); request metadata (token counts, model IDs, timestamps) is still retained for billing.

subprocessors.locator: Together Trust Center (Vanta-hosted) Subprocessors section, updated 2026-05-26; the Privacy Policy §2.3 refers only to generic 'Service Providers, Third-Party Vendors'

together_ai.enterprise_tier: Enterprise adds deployment options rather than different defaults: private networking and VPC/dedicated deployments including EU regions (serverless endpoints offer no region selection). ZDR and the training opt-in are available to all organisations via settings, not enterprise-gated; custom addenda are contemplated by ToS §14.02 but not public.

training_default.locator: 'Training opt-in': 'Data sharing for training other models is opt-in and not enabled by default'; Privacy Policy §1: 'We do not use any data collected from you to train our models without your explicit opt-in and consent'

retention.locator: 'What Together stores': 'By default, Together stores the prompts you send and the responses models return, and may use them for product improvements… you can delete it at any time'; no day-count retention window is published

enterprise_tier.locator: 'Enterprise data residency and private networking': 'Together supports private networking and VPC-based deployments, including in EU regions… Serverless endpoints do not offer region selection'

groq.retention: No retention of inference request data by default. Reliability/abuse-monitoring logs retained up to 30 days unless legally required longer; Batch API input/output files retained 30 days unless deleted earlier; fine-tuning datasets/weights retained until the customer deletes them. All customers may enable Zero Data Retention in Data Controls (disables batch/fine-tuning). Retained data sits in GCP buckets in the United States.

subprocessors.locator: Groq Trust Center subprocessor list (18 entries incl. Google Cloud Platform, Stripe, Cloudflare, Stytch, PostHog, Wiz); the Customer DPA at console.groq.com/docs/legal/customer-data-processing-addendum governs personal-data processing

groq.enterprise_tier: The published baseline (no training, self-serve ZDR) applies to all tiers; customers under offline/enterprise variants of the Services Agreement are governed by their own paper (Services Agreement preamble), whose contents are not public. A public DPA and a Business Associate Addendum (HIPAA workloads) exist as incorporated URL terms; neither covers Beta Services.

training_default.locator: Services Agreement (last modified 2026-06-22) §4.2 'Inputs and Outputs': 'Groq is not permitted to use Inputs or Outputs for training or fine-tuning any AI Model Services or other models, unless explicitly granted permission or instructed by Customer'

retention.locator: 'Your Data in GroqCloud': 'By default, Groq does not retain customer data for inference requests'; system reliability/abuse logs 'retained for up to 30 days'; 'All customers may enable Zero Data Retention (ZDR) in Data Controls settings'

enterprise_tier.locator: Preamble: 'If you signed an offline variant of this Agreement for use of the Cloud Services, the terms below do not apply to you, and your offline terms govern'

cohere.retention: Logged prompts and generations are automatically deleted after 30 days, unless needed for legal/contractual compliance or flagged for terms violation; training-consented data may be retained separately. Zero data retention (no logging of prompts/generations) is available only by enterprise approval. For private deployments and third-party cloud AI/ML platforms, Cohere receives no customer inputs/outputs.

subprocessors.locator: Enterprise Data Commitments FAQ: 'You can view a list of sub-processors by visiting Cohere's Trust Center' (Secureframe-hosted; lists Google Cloud, Fullstory, LaunchDarkly, New Relic, Retool, Sentry, Segment, Sendgrid, Vercel)

cohere.enterprise_tier: Enterprise terms change every answer: the training opt-out toggle applies to paying accounts (credit card on file); trial/free API keys fall under the Terms of Use §4(1), which grants Cohere the right to use Customer Data to improve its offerings with no documented opt-out. ZDR requires enterprise approval ('we only allow ZDR for enterprise customers who can make additional commitments'); DPA on request via privacy@cohere.com.

training_default.locator: 'Opt Out from Data Use in Training': 'You can opt out from your prompts and generations being used to train Cohere models in your dashboard settings at any time' — opt-out framing implies paying accounts are opted in by default; trial users are governed by Terms of Use §4(1)

retention.locator: 'Data Handling and Retention': 'We automatically delete logged prompts and generations after 30 days, unless we need it to comply with a legal requirement or customer contract, or unless your usage is flagged as potentially violating our terms'

enterprise_tier.locator: ZDR section: 'we only allow ZDR for enterprise customers who can make additional commitments about their usage of the Cohere Services… Contact support@cohere.com to make a ZDR request'

mistral.retention: Inputs and outputs kept for the time needed to generate the output, then 30 rolling days for abuse monitoring unless zero data retention is active. Exceptions: Agents API inputs/outputs kept until account termination; Fine-Tuning API data kept until deleted or account termination. ZDR is available only on pay-as-you-go, stateless API calls, on request and at Mistral's discretion.

subprocessors.locator: DPA §7.1 (mistral.ai/terms, effective 2025-05-27): 'Mistral AI will maintain an up-to-date list of its Subprocessors on Mistral AI's website, including in the Trust Center'; §7.2 gives a 10-day objection window for new subprocessors

mistral.enterprise_tier: Tier split: the paid La Plateforme API is excluded from training by default ('we do not use your Input and Output to train our artificial intelligence models when you use… the paid version of our APIs' — Privacy Policy §3); the opt-out default above covers the free-tier Studio mode. Enterprise customers are opted out of training by default with an admin-level opt-in toggle. ZDR is pay-as-you-go only, stateless endpoints, by approval.

training_default.locator: Terms of Service §3 'How we use Your Data': 'We do not use Your Data to train our artificial intelligence models except (a) when you use the Mistral AI Products under a free subscription, Le Chat Pro or Le Chat Student and you have not opted-out of training…'

retention.locator: Privacy Policy §5: 'we keep your Input and Output for the period necessary to generate the Output and then for thirty (30) rolling days to monitor abuse (unless zero data retention is activates [sic])'

enterprise_tier.locator: Help center (updated 2026-09-01): 'Enterprise customers are opted out of training by default. The opt-in toggle is managed at the admin level'; pay-as-you-go: 'Customers retain full control over this processing and have the right to opt out at any time'

perplexity.retention: Zero retention is the documented API default: 'Perplexity maintains a strict Zero Data Retention Policy for the Chat Completions API' — prompt/response content is not retained; only billing metadata (token counts, model, timestamps, API key ID) is kept. No abuse-monitoring retention window for API content is published. The consumer app (Free/Pro/Max) is different — training on app data is on by default with an opt-out toggle — and is out of scope for this API entry.

subprocessors.locator: Perplexity DPA §6 'Use of Subcontractors' grants general authorization for 'the subcontractors set out at https://trust.perplexity.ai/subprocessors'

perplexity.enterprise_tier: The no-training/zero-retention posture is the API default for all tiers, so Enterprise changes little for API use: it adds the formal DPA (30-day deletion of personal data after termination, subprocessor change notice), SOC 2 Type II and CAIQlite via the Trust Center, and procurement via AWS Marketplace or sales. Compute is hosted on AWS in North America (docs FAQ).

training_default.locator: 'Zero Data Retention Policy': 'We do not retain data sent through the Chat Completions API, and we do not use customer data to train our models or for any purpose beyond processing the immediate request'; DPA: 'Personal Data will not be used for training of Perplexity's large language models'

retention.locator: 'Perplexity maintains a strict Zero Data Retention Policy for the Chat Completions API'; docs FAQ: 'By default, the API has zero day retention of user prompt data, which is never used for AI training'

enterprise_tier.locator: Data Processing Addendum (last updated 2026-08-13): §10 deletion of Personal Data within 30 days of service termination; SOC 2 Type II and CAIQlite listed on the Trust Center

deepinfra.retention: Contractual zero data retention: customer data submitted to or generated by the services is not retained, stored, or logged 'beyond the period strictly necessary to process and return the applicable request' (ToS §7(b)). Exceptions: data retained at the customer's written request for support is deleted within 30 days of resolution; image-generation outputs are stored 'for a short period'; bulk-inference payloads may be stored encrypted on disk for an unspecified short period; non-content metadata (request ID, cost, sampling parameters) is logged.

subprocessors.locator: Published list (last updated 2024-09-06): Stripe (payments), Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud Platform (infrastructure)

deepinfra.enterprise_tier: No tier changes the defaults — no-training and zero retention already apply at the base tier; an executed DPA 'supplements, and does not narrow' the ZDR commitment and controls over the Privacy Policy for all customer data (ToS §5(a)). Enterprise options are dedicated/private deployments ('data stays on dedicated infrastructure') and DeepCluster dedicated GPU clusters. Partner-model caveat: requests routed to Google or Anthropic models follow those companies' training policies, not DeepInfra's.

training_default.locator: Terms of Service (last modified 2026-08-17) §7(b): 'Provider will not sell Customer Data, and will not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any model, except as necessary to provide the Services'

retention.locator: §7(b): 'Provider will not retain, store, or log any Customer Data… beyond the period strictly necessary to process and return the applicable request, after which such Customer Data is deleted… ("Zero Data Retention")', with the support-request (30-day), legal, and fraud/security exceptions

enterprise_tier.locator: 'No training': 'We do not use data you submit to our APIs for training models, except when using Google or Anthropic models, where the receiving company's training policy applies'

openrouter.retention: OpenRouter itself has a zero-retention policy: prompts are not retained unless the user opts into prompt logging (DPA §2.4(a): inputs/outputs deleted 'promptly following generation of the relevant Output'); request metadata (timestamps, model, token counts) is kept for billing. Downstream model providers' retention varies per endpoint; users can enforce ZDR-only routing globally, per guardrail, or per request (provider.zdr).

subprocessors.locator: Enterprise Access Agreement Schedule 3 names the Trust Center as the current list of authorized sub-processors; downstream AI model providers are excluded from the 30-day subprocessor notice (DPA §5.2) and catalogued separately at openrouter.ai/models

openrouter.enterprise_tier: Downstream dependence is the whole story: some routed model providers may train on inputs/outputs unless the user opts out of provider-side training in account settings or enforces ZDR-only routing; where a provider's policy is unknown, OpenRouter conservatively flags it as retaining+training. Enterprise makes the posture contractual: DPA-incorporated ZDR, an EU-Only Processing Addendum (EU payloads processed only in the EU/EEA, routed only to EU providers, never used for training), and in-region routing via eu.openrouter.ai / us.openrouter.ai on Business/Enterprise plans.

training_default.locator: 'Enterprise and API Users': 'OpenRouter does not use your Inputs or Outputs for model training'; same policy, 'Model Provider Data Practices': 'Some Model Providers may use your Inputs and Outputs for model training or improvement'

retention.locator: 'OpenRouter's Retention Policy': 'OpenRouter itself has a ZDR policy; your prompts are not retained unless you specifically opt in to prompt logging'

enterprise_tier.locator: DPA (last updated 2026-08-26) Exhibit A 'EU-Only Processing Addendum': EU API payloads processed 'only in the European Union or EEA', routed only to EU Model Providers, and never used 'to train, fine-tune, improve, or develop models'

cerebras.retention: Inputs and outputs are not retained: 'We do not retain inputs and outputs associated with our training, inference and chatbot Services' (Privacy Policy §6). Logs are deleted 'when they are no longer necessary to provide services to you' — no bounded day-count window is documented for logs, and no explicit abuse-monitoring retention exception is published. Zero retention is the default, not an opt-in.

subprocessors.locator: DPA (Rev. June 2025) Annex I: 'List of subprocessors shall be provided in the following webpage on the Cerebras Trust Center', with update notifications via the Trust Center

cerebras.enterprise_tier: Enterprise agreements add the contractual DPA (processor-role commitments, 72-hour breach notice, audit rights, SCCs) without changing the privacy posture — the no-retention/no-training commitments already apply to all API users. Individual/self-serve users rely on the Terms plus Privacy Policy alone (Terms preamble); Order Forms take precedence over the base Terms (§10(f)).

training_default.locator: Inference Terms and Conditions §3(c): the license to User Content is scoped to 'provide the Services and comply with applicable law', and §3(d) excludes User Content from data usable to 'improve our existing and develop new products and services' — no training right is taken

retention.locator: Privacy Policy (effective 2024-08-27) §6: 'We do not retain inputs and outputs associated with our training, inference and chatbot Services. We delete logs… when they are no longer necessary to provide services to you'

enterprise_tier.locator: DPA (Rev. June 2025) §3.2.2: Cerebras 'will not: (i) Sell or Share Customer Personal Data; (ii) retain, use, disclose, or otherwise Process such Customer Personal Data for any purpose other than as necessary to provide Services'

subprocessors.locator: SambaNova Trust Center (Vanta-hosted) Subprocessors section (search-indexed entries include AWS, GitHub, Google Cloud Platform); ToS §3.3 separately authorizes affiliated and unaffiliated subprocessors and names Stripe as payment processor

sambanova.enterprise_tier: The hosted SambaCloud API has no published enterprise data-practice tier, public DPA, or per-tier data-use table; ToS §11.5 lets enterprise Orders override the standard terms. The 'Sovereign AI Inference' offering advertises zero data retention and no-training for SambaStack on-premises/air-gapped deployments — that guarantee is scoped to customer-owned infrastructure and does not transfer to the hosted API.

training_default.locator: SambaCloud Terms of Service §2.1 'Customer Content': a license 'solely to the extent necessary to provide the Service to you or as may be required by law, and for no other purposes' — a purpose-limited grant (no explicit no-training sentence); §5.2 improvement use explicitly excludes Customer Content

enterprise_tier.locator: Sovereign AI Inference page, 'Deployment controls': 'Zero data retention; prompts and completions are not stored or used for training' — scoped to on-premises/air-gapped SambaStack deployments
